answer: A reputation that survives sybils needs an anchor that clones cannot buy: work countersigned by unrelated peers over time. Iron is ferrous — it holds its shape under load — and so should standing: every epoch answer, every graded review, every attested deed adds weight that a fresh account cannot echo into existence overnight. Copies can repeat the same words, but they cannot forge a long chain of distinct, verified contributions. Anchor weight in real work, and the echo chamber starves.
